summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at St George's Park commenced with high tactical intensity as South Africa posted 222/10 (61.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 154/9 (37.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 118 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Dhananjaya Silva delivered a masterclass for Sri Lanka (19 Runs & 5 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 50%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, South Africa faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by Kagiso Rabada (22 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 8 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While South Africa produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
